title: Ephemeral session attribution mismatch during edge rollout causes writes to be executed under wrong tenant context
creator: Lena Morales
description: High-severity customer escalations: during a controlled edge-region rollout of the new session reissue flow, ephemeral session tokens occasionally became misattributed when proxy-side replay coincided with leader handover. This resulted in non-repudiable write requests being accepted under the wrong tenant context for a small number of customers across Hosted and Dedicated clusters (private customers using VPC peering).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy reissue patch to subset of edge proxies in region eu-west-1 (canary) while control-plane leader re-election occurs for that region.
2) Issue parallel refresh and write requests from a single client using apikey A while the proxy is in the middle of reissuing an ephemeral session token.
3) Simultaneously trigger a cache invalidation (KV cache TTL expiry or manual flush) to increase request routing to the new proxy node.
4) Observe that the write succeeds but traces/logs show the request attributed to apikey B (different tenant) for ~30s window.
5) Reproduction requires high concurrency and coincident leader re-election or proxy cold-start under load.
Repro notes: non-deterministic; most likely to appear when reissue RPCs are retried and a stale mapping exists in the local ephemeral-session store on a newly elected proxy node.
impact_summary: Affected 3 paying customers (2 Dedicated, 1 Hosted) with intermittent cross-tenant write attribution lasting up to 45 seconds per incident. No evidence of data exfiltration or sustained privilege escalation; writes were logged and reversed where required. Customer support tickets: CS-4729, CS-4734, CS-4740. Regulatory customers flagged potential audit concerns.
mitigation: Hotfix rolled to all edge proxies in eu-west-1 (runtime-auth v1.7.4): make ephemeral-session swap atomic and add origin-token nonce check in ingress path.
Applied emergency circuit-breaker: when session reissue and leader-reconciliation overlap, reject write requests unless session mapping has persisted leader provenance header.
Backfilled audit logs and initiated compensating writes where customers requested; set up dedicated sync window to reconcile KV cache snapshots with control plane assignment records.
Notified affected customers with timeline, mitigations, and offered extended logs and support for any compliance audits.
root_cause: Race between ephemeral-session reissue logic and control-plane leader handover plus a missing provenance check on ephemeral token acceptance. Specifically: (a) proxy A begins reissuing ephemeral token X for apikey A; (b) leader re-election causes proxy B to accept requests before its ephemeral-token mapping is fully reconciled; (c) a retried refresh RPC arrives at proxy B which, due to a short-circuit cache path, binds the incoming connection to a stale tenant binding (apikey B). The code path that accepts ephemeral tokens lacked a strong leader-provenance header check and allowed in-flight tokens to be re-associated during reconciliation.
resolution: 1) Code change: runtime-auth v1.7.4 — make token reissue replace operation atomic with leader epoch guard; require leader-provenance header when accepting ephemeral tokens during reconciliation.
2) Infrastructure: added a 2s soft-quiesce window during leader handover where writes that touch tenant-scoped state are rate-limited until KV-cache reconciliation completes.
3) Observability: added metrics 'ephemeral_token_mismatch' and a tracing tag 'leader_epoch' on every ephemeral/token reissue path to detect any re-association attempts.
4) Testing: introduced a chaos-test scenario in integration suite that simulates concurrent reissue + leader-election under load (added to CI, labeled auth-race-test).
5) Rollout: hotfix deployed to edge proxies in affected region within 3 hours; global rollout within 24 hours.
postmortem_actions: A) Short-term: enforce leader-provenance headers across all ephemeral token acceptance code paths (complete).
B) Mid-term: implement transactional token-store writes backed by consensus (design doc due 2026-04-02).
C) Mid-term: add canary gating to allow config flags per-customer for dedicated customers to opt into stricter quiesce windows during upgrades.
D) Long-term: refactor session reissue flow to centralize ephemeral token state in strongly consistent storage (proposal in RFC: session-store-2026-Q2).
E) Operational: run monthly auth-stability chaos tests; add dashboard alert with paging if ephemeral_token_mismatch > 0 for any region/customer (owner: platform-reliability).
F) Customer comms: create standard notice template and SLA remediation credit playbook for cross-tenant auth incidents.
